rappel_detail.anchor: anchor at the top of the easy summit slab
rappel_detail.station: From the summit, scramble down to the top of the easy slab.
rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 1 of 8, single rope, to the col at the top of #2 Gully.

rappel_detail.station: Scramble from the col to the bolted station on the east side of #2 Gully.
rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 2 of 8, the first of about four double-rope rappels (two 60 m ropes) down #2 Gully.

rappel_detail.anchor: tree or chockstone with old slings
rappel_detail.station: After traversing a long stretch of slab, up to 100 yards, on the east side of the gully.
hazards: Slings here date back decades; back them up or replace them.

rappel_detail.anchor: tree or chockstone with old slings
rappel_detail.station: The next station down the east side of the gully, after another slab traverse.

rappel_detail.anchor: tree or chockstone with old slings
rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 5 of 8, double-rope. Near the base of the gully, pack the ropes and downclimb.
hazards: The west-side rock near the base of the gully is the loosest on the descent; a party member was struck by a 500 lb block that came loose under hand pressure in 2001.

rappel_detail.station: The steep section of the wooded ramp, reached after crossing back over the Y Notch and the Key Ledge Traverse.
rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 6 of 8, single rope, off the steep part of the ramp. Continue down past the Glade Saddle.

rappel_detail.anchor: anchor at the top of the lower slab
rappel_detail.station: The top of the lower slab.
rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 7 of 8, double-rope, down the slab.

rappel_detail.anchor: anchor partway down the lower slab
rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 8 of 8, double-rope, to the base of the slab.

set.rappels: About 8 rappels: one single-rope from the summit slab to the col, about four double-rope (two 60 m ropes) down #2 Gully, one single-rope off the wooded ramp, and two double-rope down the lower slab
